title: Hilltop Access Road, Kennewick, Washington
description: An example road plan: a single-lane gravel access road for maintenance trucks, from the end of the road stub off W 47th Ave at the foot of a hill at the south edge of Kennewick, Washington, to a level site on the hilltop. The plan illustrates Roadie on USGS lidar terrain - it isn't a proposed project.

**The site.** From "Road end" (elevation 933 feet) to "Hilltop" (elevation 1,137 feet). The straight line between them climbs 204 feet in 1,092 feet (18.7%) - steeper than the maximum grade, so a road is longer than the straight line.
**Design criteria.** Maximum grade 12%, minimum curve radius 50 feet, maximum retaining wall height 20 feet.
**Features added to the site.** They aren't the USGS's - verify them in the field:
- Streams: West draw, East draw
- Existing roads: Hilltop track
- Exclusion areas: House lots
The USGS maps show no streams or roads on the hill, so these are from the lidar terrain and the topographic map:
- The West draw (10.6 acres of the hill drain to it) and the East draw (4.4 acres) are draws of the hill's north face. Both options cross the East draw, with a culvert.

- The Hilltop track is an unmapped dirt track up the hill's east shoulder to the hilltop - its worn trough shows in the lidar terrain. Whether the road may use it, and its condition, must be verified in the field.
- The House lots are the house lots west of the road end, which the road must stay off - their extent is an assumption, from the buildings on the topographic map.

**Options not kept.** A road west across the West draw (cost score 288.6, with an 18 foot cut) and two roads up the middle of the north face (cost scores 255.1 and 380.2 - each nearly twice as long) cost much more than the options kept, and depend on nothing the kept options don't.

**Limitations.** The terrain is the USGS 3D Elevation Program's lidar ground elevations, and the streams, roads, and trails are the USGS National Map's. What they lack - buildings, property lines, utilities, and unmapped roads and drainages - isn't in the plan unless it was added. Turnarounds aren't modeled. The cost scores compare the options - they aren't bid estimates.
The turnaround at the hilltop isn't modeled, and property lines aren't known. The Hilltop track is steeper than the plan's maximum grade (see the Existing Roads option).

sources.name: USGS 3D Elevation Program 1 meter elevation model WA_ColumbiaValley_2018_D19

options.name: Existing Roads
description: The least-cost option - its cost score is 146.6. It's 2,118 feet long and 14 feet wide, gravel, and its new road's maximum grade is 11%.

A new road climbs east from the road end across the hill's north face (its side slopes are 25% to 55%), crosses the East draw, and comes around the hill's east shoulder to the Hilltop track. It follows the track to the hilltop, where its last 190 feet are new road.
- **Existing road.** It follows Hilltop track for 440 feet (stations 14+85 to 19+25) - as built, its grade averages 13.8%, and 18.3% over its steepest 50 feet, which is over the 12% maximum grade.
- **Existing road upgrade.** An existing road is costed as an upgrade, with no earthwork - verify its width, grade, and surface in the field.
- **Structures.** 1 culvert (East draw culvert, station 6+05, 3 ft), 4 turnouts.
- **Earthwork.** 1,690 cy of cut and 1,493 cy of fill, with 22 cy of borrow (import). Its deepest cut is 4.6 feet (station 5+02). Its deepest fill is 6.9 feet (station 10+95).
- **Cost.** Its largest items: surfacing (gravel) 45.0, common excavation 25.8, ditches and cross drains 23.0.
- **Design warnings.** None.
Verify in the field whether maintenance trucks can use the track as it's built - it's steeper than the maximum grade. If they can't, the New Road option is the fallback.

options.name: New Road
description: It costs 31% more than the least-cost option, "Existing Roads" - its cost score is 192.7. It's 2,280 feet long and 14 feet wide, gravel, and its maximum grade is 11%.

An all-new road, for comparison - the same climb across the north face and around the east shoulder, then its own line below the Hilltop track, to the hilltop from the southeast. All of it is within the design grade. It costs more than the Existing Roads option because its last 800 feet are new road where that option upgrades the track.
- **Structures.** 2 culverts (Sag cross drain, station 5+79, 1.5 ft; East draw culvert, station 6+14, 3 ft), 5 turnouts.
- **Earthwork.** 2,229 cy of cut and 470 cy of fill, with 1,469 cy of waste (export). Its deepest cut is 3.7 feet (station 7+83). Its deepest fill is 2.6 feet (station 6+16).
- **Cost.** Its largest items: surfacing (gravel) 60.8, common excavation 34.1, ditches and cross drains 31.3.
- **Design warnings.** None.
